newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls for aggressive probe of Moscow murder.
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls for aggressive probe of Moscow murder.

text.p: The United States called on Russia on Monday to mount a "very aggressive investigation" into the suspected contract murder of an American businessman in Moscow.
Paul Tatum, 39, of Edmond, Oklahoma, was killed outside a subway station on Sunday afternoon by an assailant firing a Kalashnikov submachine gun.

"The United States deplores the murder of Mr. Tatum," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said. "We are working with the Russian government to try to make sure that the Russian government mounts a very aggressive investigation, a criminal investigation into this brutal murder of an American citizen."

Burns told a news briefing the U.S. Embassy in Moscow had been working on the case with the Russian government, police officials and the Moscow municipal government. He said it was at least the second time an American businessman had been murdered in Moscow in recent years "and we are very, very concerned about it."
Tatum had been fighting a legal battle with Moscow city authorities over control of one of the city's major hotels, the Radisson-Slavjanskaya.

Burns said he could not say if the United States would send any American law enforcement officials to Russia to work on the case. Such a step would probably come only if the Russian government requested it.
